checked_sources: Independent modular congruence versus prefix replay over 1..120000
correctness.rationale: R(n) is coprime to 10; the least prime p dividing a qualifying n>1 must be 3, since otherwise the nontrivial order of 10 modulo p divides both n and p-1. For each p_i>3 all prime factors of its order are smaller than p_i, giving the required prefix including exponents. Conversely, the tests imply ord_{p_i}(10)|n and it is prime to p_i. Odd-prime LTE supplies v_{p_i}(R(n))>=e_i+1 and v_3(R(n))=v_3(n); n=1 is separate. The exact two-prime condition follows. The primitive orders can also be checked without exceptions from Bang–Zsigmondy: for b=10^{3^{a-1}}, b^2+b+1 has 3-adic valuation one and gcd with b-1 equal to 3, hence has a prime q>3 with order 3^a for 10. Odd orders force all prime divisors into the stated quadratic splitting set, including 3. Squaring the containing set's Euler product gives zeta(s)L(s,chi)(1-2^{-s})(1-5^{-s}) times the product over chi(p)=-1; the regular factor at s=1 is positive and gives C_40 after taking its square root and dividing by Gamma(1/2). Multiplication by 3 bijects this semigroup with its multiples of 3, giving the factor 1/3. A separate bounded replay factored n and compared the prefix tests with pow(10,n,9*n)==1 over 1..120000: 27 agreements on hits and no mismatches; four seed primes with three exponents each were also checked. This is finite corroboration, not the proof. No asymptotic equality for A(X) is asserted.
residual_risks: The displayed asymptotic equivalence is for the containing semigroup only; the actual counting function is subject to substantially stronger prior upper bounds.

evidence: The 2012 paper defines N_u as the indices dividing their corresponding recurrence term. For simple roots and a nondegenerate recurrence of order 2, Theorem 1.1 bounds its count by c_0(2) X/log X. The recurrence u_{n+2}=11u_{n+1}-10u_n has simple roots 10 and 1 with ratio not a root of unity, so the hypotheses hold. It has gcd(11,-10)=1 and the stated initial conditions, so the Lucas-specific Theorem 1.2 applies as well. Smyth Theorem 1 gives the prime-extension rule for all Lucas parameters and includes basic starting values; only 1 is basic here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: There is no loss of domain or change of counted variable: N_u(X)=A(X). The earlier estimate asymptotically dominates any positive constant times X/sqrt(log X), explicitly including C_40/3. The prime-extension theorem covers more than this decimal instance.

evidence: In Smyth Theorem 1(a) the allowed next primes from m in the set are the primes dividing u_m Delta. Here Delta=81, hence starting from 1 only 3 may be added; for p>3 the extension condition is p|R(m), equivalent to ord_p(10)|m. Theorem 3 permits successively removing largest prime factors, since every qualifying n is odd and the even exceptional forms do not occur. Equivalently one may reorder by smaller primes, because the order divides p-1 and cannot require p or a larger prime. Iterating this gives exactly the prefix test and its sufficiency with repeated powers. Restricting it to one prime beyond 3 gives the two-support formula, and the cited primitive-divisor theorem at exponent 3^a gives infinitely many such primes immediately. The prior O(X/log X) bound implies A(X)/(X/sqrt(log X)) tends to zero.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The frozen conditions are not merely vaguely similar to prior work: the algebraic parameter substitution, ordering rule, and valuation exceptions match. The exact C_40 calculation is for a textbook fixed-character Euler product of a proper overcounting set, not a nontrivial improvement to the earlier bound on the reviewed lengths.

originality.rationale: Established prior coverage, not an access issue. Smyth's general Lucas-index classification specializes mechanically to the prime-prefix and two-support descriptions. The same count A(X) is a direct case of Alba González–Luca–Pomerance–Shparlinski, whose Theorem 1.1 gives O(X/log X), already o(X/sqrt(log X)); their Lucas-specific Theorem 1.2 is stronger still. The exact constant of the larger containing set does not recover an original bound on A(X).
residual_risks: This decision does not establish earliest priority for every elementary component. The verified published coverage suffices irrespective of incomplete secondary searches.

value.rationale: The subject is natural, but the exact arithmetic classification is a mechanical Lucas specialization, and the claimed logarithmic upper bound is substantially weaker than the existing estimate for the same A(X). The exact coefficient measures only an elementary containing semigroup, not the sought lengths or a sharp obstruction for them. The two-prime family is a useful illustration of the rule but follows immediately from classical primitive divisors and does not leave an independently valuable new claim to repair here.
residual_risks: The failed disposition is not a finding that the mathematics or the finite regression is false. No revised result is claimed.
